A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same distributional-scaling study despite the revised title. Text, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support matching retained, added, and removed material.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments across random seeds on counting, reverse-order addition, and continued pretraining of Qwen models evaluated on MMLU.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds CommonsenseQA results and loss-based analyses of synthetic-task performance distributions.

M1.justification: Both versions use decoder-only Transformers with RoPE for the synthetic tasks and reinitialize Qwen's final attention layer and LM head before full-parameter continued pretraining. The additional benchmark and evaluation metrics do not establish a changed model or training procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds CommonsenseQA as a second natural-language benchmark (Appendix E.1, Figure 14). It also removes the multi-test-length evaluations for counting and addition reported in v1 Figures 11–12, retaining the principal fixed-length cases. Together these substantially revise documented evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: The matched MMLU comparisons retain the random-guess reference and original Qwen2.5-0.5B and Qwen2.5-1.5B base-model references. CommonsenseQA reuses the existing model-scale comparison and random-guess reference; no new competing method is introduced.

E3.justification: v3 adds evaluation using the mean across sequences of maximum per-token loss (Equation 1). The new CommonsenseQA experiment uses 50%, 70%, 80%, 90%, and 100% task-data mixtures and compares model sizes at 80%. Previously stated training budgets and hyperparameters for retained experiments remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The continuous-metric robustness investigation expands from minimum-probability histograms to additional loss-based distribution analyses for both synthetic tasks (v3 Figures 6 and 13). Conversely, v1's two multi-length generalization sweeps disappear. This materially revises the supplementary evidence, while retaining the one-layer capacity check.

E5.justification: v3 adds explicitly reported kernel-density estimates for the loss-based robustness checks, extending v1's histogram-based continuous-metric analysis. The stated 250 counting seeds, 200 addition seeds, 20 MMLU reinitializations, and 95% confidence intervals using 1000 bootstrap samples remain unchanged; no increase in repeated runs is stated.

E6.justification: New CommonsenseQA results show the 0.5B model clustering near 0% and 20% accuracy at an 80% data mixture, while the 1.5B model concentrates near 20% (Figure 14). Loss distributions are added and multi-length result entries removed. Matched minimum-probability plots change from roughly 10^-4 values to a 0–1 scale without explanation. Retained MMLU findings remain stable.

T1.justification: v3 introduces a mathematical definition of the loss-based error measure in Equation 1. Equation 2 formalizes the minimum-probability metric already described in v1, and Appendix B's breakthroughness and linearity definitions remain unchanged. No new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: Both versions attribute apparent breakthroughs to changing bimodal performance distributions, distinguish abrupt modal improvement from gradual distributional change, and explain the counting task's inverse scaling through success probability. The additional experiments support these retained core claims.

C2.justification: v3 explains why worst-token statistics expose rare errors and discusses the counting task's more diffuse failure cluster under loss-based measurement (Appendix D). Section 6 drops the specific call to validate bimodality during LM pretraining from scratch, although the existing continued-pretraining and latent-capability qualifications remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly states that synthetic experiments can run on a single 40GB A100 with gradient accumulation, taking up to two hours for counting and six hours for addition. These are additional resource disclosures, rather than evidence of changed training settings.

R1.justification: v3 adds Talmor et al.'s CommonsenseQA reference and removes Gopalani et al.'s matrix-completion study and its discussion. The broader positioning around random variation, emergence, length generalization, and depth-versus-width scaling remains substantially the same.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, several explanatory passages, and related-work paragraphs undergo widespread rewriting and compression. The title and terminology change, Methodology becomes Experiments, the appendices are reorganized into more specific sections, and the Impact Statement is removed.

P2.justification: v3 changes the main text from two columns to one, rearranges summary-statistic panels into horizontal rows, combines the two Wasserstein plots into Figure 4, and moves counting histograms to the appendix. New loss and CommonsenseQA figures, removed multi-length plots, and revised axes and captions substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The additional CommonsenseQA evidence, explicitly defined loss-based robustness checks, and GPU/runtime disclosures modestly strengthen empirical support and reproducibility. The gain is limited because v1 already included continuous-metric checks, while v3 removes multi-length evidence and leaves the probability rescaling unexplained. The need for validation through pretraining larger models from scratch remains unresolved.
